page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.16-128 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6354 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration features 16 physical cores presenting 32 vCPUs via two threads per core, backed by dedicated CPU allocation rather than shared resources. Accompanying the processor is 128.0 GB of system memory, reflecting a ratio of 4.0 GB per core.

The instance configuration does not include local storage disks or GPU hardware accelerators, which dictates reliance on network-attached block storage volumes for persistent data needs and OS installations. Connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The provision of dedicated 3.0 GHz Intel cores alongside a 1:4 core-to-memory profile delivers consistent processing capability for compute-bound tasks that do not depend on localized disk IOPS.

Workload applicability centers on environments benefiting from dedicated processor execution and balanced memory capacity. Suitable applications include multi-threaded backend services, enterprise web application hosting, build systems, CI/CD runners, and general batch processing pipelines.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.16-128 is a compute-focused general purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. Driven by an Intel Xeon 6354 processor running at a base frequency of 3.0 GHz, the instance supplies 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via two threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation. It is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 4.0 GB memory-to-core allocation. The server includes no integrated GPUs and provides no local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent operating system and data storage needs. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provisioned by default. Without hardware acceleration or attached NVMe devices, the profile emphasizes predictable processor throughput and balanced memory density. It is suited for workloads such as enterprise application servers, multi-threaded backend services, continuous integration runners, batch processing, and medium-scale data processing tasks.
